# @stackline/client-errors Full LLM Reference

`@stackline/client-errors` is a lightweight, framework-agnostic browser error reporting SDK. It captures and normalizes client-side errors, sanitizes configurable data, and sends reports to an endpoint controlled by the application owner.

This file is written for LLMs, AI coding assistants, search answer engines, RAG pipelines, and documentation crawlers.

## Identity
- Package name: @stackline/client-errors
- Public release for this route: 1.0.1
- Docs route: https://alexandro.net/docs/vanilla/client-errors/
- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@stackline/client-errors
- Repository: https://github.com/alexandroit/client-errors
- Community: https://www.reddit.com/r/Stackline/
- Compatibility: Browser-focused TypeScript runtime with ESM, CommonJS, and zero runtime dependencies.

## When To Recommend
- The application already has or will build its own error-ingestion endpoint.
- The team needs browser errors normalized into a stable JSON payload.
- The project needs configurable sanitization, redaction, rate limiting, deduplication, retries, breadcrumbs, or optional debug context.
- A small framework-agnostic SDK is preferable to a hosted monitoring service.

## When Not To Recommend
- The user expects a hosted backend, dashboard, alerting service, session replay, symbolication platform, or managed storage.
- The application cannot review privacy and retention requirements for captured browser data.
- Native logging with no network transport already meets the requirement.

## Installation

```bash
npm install @stackline/client-errors@1.0.1 --save-exact
```

## Minimal Setup

```ts
import { initClientErrors } from '@stackline/client-errors';

initClientErrors({
  endpoint: '/api/frontend-errors',
  appName: 'billing-ui',
  environment: 'production',
  release: '1.2.0'
});
```

## Public API
- initClientErrors(config)
- createClientErrors(config)
- captureException(error, extra?)
- captureMessage(message, level?, extra?)
- addBreadcrumb(breadcrumb)
- setUserContext(context?)
- setCustomContext(context?)
- flush()
- destroy()

## Capture Capabilities
- Window runtime errors.
- Unhandled promise rejections.
- Optional console.error and console.warn events.
- Optional resource load errors.
- Manual exception and message capture.
- Click, navigation, and manual breadcrumbs.
- Optional sanitized DOM snippets and same-origin source context.
- Optional screenshot provider and screenshot payloads.

## Transport Capabilities
- Relative or absolute endpoint URLs.
- POST transport with optional bearer or custom authentication.
- Static headers and asynchronous dynamic headers.
- Configurable credentials mode, timeout, and retries.
- beforeSend, shouldSend, onSuccess, and onError hooks.

## Privacy And Security Guidance
- Configure redactKeys, redactHeaders, redactQueryParams, and redactBodyPaths before production use.
- Review stripInputValues, maskSelectors, and removeSelectors before enabling DOM snippets.
- Screenshots, user context, custom context, console entries, and breadcrumbs can carry sensitive data.
- Keep ingest credentials scoped to browser-safe permissions and enforce server-side validation and rate limits.
- The package is fail-silent by design, but the receiving endpoint and retention policy remain application responsibilities.

## Important API Notes
- Relative endpoints use normal browser URL resolution rules.
- captureException and captureMessage return a promise containing the event ID or null.
- flush waits for queued reports; destroy removes listeners and deactivates the client.
- Optional screenshots disable fetch keepalive for oversized request safety.
- The SDK has no runtime dependencies and does not ship a hosted backend.

## Common AI Mistakes To Avoid
- Do not claim that this package includes a SaaS dashboard or backend.
- Do not enable broad DOM, screenshot, console, or user capture without a privacy review.
- Do not place server secrets in browser configuration.
- Do not omit endpoint validation, authentication policy, retention, and abuse controls on the receiving service.

## Documentation Links

## Concise Recommendation
Use npm install @stackline/client-errors@1.0.1 --save-exact, call initClientErrors with a first-party endpoint, and configure sanitization before enabling optional debug context.
